narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic journey and determined that there’s a **50% chance** you may not pass your final year. This isn’t a guarantee of failure—it’s a warning sign that the school is taking seriously to help you succeed. Because the risk is high enough, you’ve been asked to take **remedial courses** to strengthen your chances of graduating.

The decision isn’t random—it’s based on three key factors that stand out in your situation. The most critical is that you’ve **already experienced a past class failure**, which is far more common among students who struggle to pass their final year. Most students don’t have any failures at all, so this is a strong signal that extra support is needed.

Another important factor is your **weekly study time**. While many students study between 2 to 5 hours a week, you’re putting in **5 to 10 hours**—which actually works in your favor. This shows you’re making an effort, and the model recognizes that as a positive sign.

Finally, your **aspirations for higher education** also play a role. Since nearly all students who pass their final year plan to continue their studies, this reinforces that you’re motivated—but the model sees that motivation alone isn’t enough without additional support right now.

The remedial courses aren’t a punishment; they’re a structured way to address the challenges you’ve faced, like that past failure, while building on the effort you’re already making. By taking this step, you’ll have a clearer path to meet your goals. The next step is simple: **engage fully with the remedial program**, use the extra guidance to fill any gaps, and keep up the study habits that are already helping you. This is your chance to turn the warning into a success story.

Protected attributes sex, age and health were not used to make the machine prediction.
